question: In 1856, Berthelot synthesised which compound by the reaction of a mixture of sulfated hydrogen with carbon disulfide on red-hot copper?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Methane**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 1856, Berthelot synthesised the Methane compound by the reaction of a mixture of sulfated hydrogen with carbon disulfide on red-hot copper.
 
• When a mixture of CS₂​ & H₂​S is passed over heated **copper methane gas is produced.**
 
• Methane is emitted during the production and transport of coal, natural gas, and oil. 
 
• Methane emissions also result from livestock and other agricultural practices and from the decay of organic waste in municipal solid waste landfills.
 
• In 2018, methane (CH₄) accounted for about 9.5 percent of all U.S. greenhouse gas emissions from human activities.
 
• Human activities emitting methane include leaks from natural gas systems and the raising of livestock.
 
• Methane is also emitted by natural sources such as natural wetlands. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is a colourless, highly flammable, and easily liquefied gas.
 
• In the abundance of oxygen, it forms Carbon dioxide, but if limited oxygen is available, then it forms Carbon Monoxide.
